Regions are disjoint, so the order of the parts changes nothing; the battlefield oracles (Oracle:city, castle, mine, special) compare whole turned maps.

The original turns the 40x40 cells in place, a quarter at a time (si < 0x14: 20 x 20 four-cycles, rows by stride 0x28/0xA0), and tests the mirror itself (cmp [bp+0xA], 4: r >= 4). TurnCells turns from a copy of the level over all 40x40 cells, and Apply passes mirror = r >= 4. Same cells moved: the city oracle (CityOracleTests, the original city_build, which turns its map through R004+0x21BA) compares the built levels byte for byte.

Each of the five functions tests r == 1/5, 2/6, 3/7 (a dec ladder over r = 0..7 picking the same three arms), r >= 4 for the mirror (0x2988, 0x2E39, 0x30E7, 0x328B, 0x35C1), its record count (+0x2184, +0x2FB6, +0x300C, +0x3326) as a loop, and in R004+0x2F54 the exit-target flag [bp+0xC]. MapTurn has these as q = r & 3 with switch 1/2/3 in TurnPointAt/TurnBox, mirror = r >= 4, the count loops in Apply, and turnExitTargets; facing_turn(f, r%4) then facing_turn(.., 4) equals TurnFacing(f, r).

TurnBox is the port's one copy of the box turn that R004+0x29B0 does inline (it calls nothing): checked 0x2A08..0x2B2D: x = word/4 signed, y = word/2, w = byte+4 >> 2, h = byte+5 >> 1, quarter turn 1 writes (0x140-y-h)<<2, x<<1 and the bytes h<<2, w<<1, as TurnBox case 1 (wordSizes false); the negated-x flag is undone/redone around it as in TurnDoor. R004+0x2F54 is cited by TurnBox as the same code.

That is the n-th set formula in ascending order: KnownBits enumerates formula f as bit 1 << (f % 3) of byte f / 3, and NthFormula takes Order().Skip(n).First. Out-of-range n (AX left as DS) can not come: ClickListLine returns when line + top >= the list count.

R031+0x433C walks 0x11 saint bytes (2E38:082C + member*0x14) testing 0x80 >> bit for bits 0..7, counting n down, and returns byte*8 + bit (0x4371..0x4394): the n-th known saint below 136 in ascending order. NthSaint is Saints.Where(i < 136).Order().Skip(n).First, KnownBits holding saint s as 0x80 >> (s & 7) of byte s >> 3. As for formulas, n is always below the list count (ClickListLine).
